title: What they said at the time

clips.q: This is a company’s dream… We’re happy because he’s captured their pocketbooks, too.
clips.who: **Julie Wainwright**, to Forbes, on the sock puppet, as quoted in Slate, Jun 2000[^14]

clips.q: It looks an awful lot like they’ve built that brand for a lousy business.
clips.who: **Slate**, “The Puppet That Ate a Dot-Com,” Jun 6, 2000[^14]
**CNET News.com** headline on IPO day, Feb 2000[^12]

clips.q: Shipping huge bags of dog food doesn’t sound like a great profit opportunity.
Out of the more than 50 prospects contacted, fewer than 8 were even prepared to visit with the company.
I am deeply saddened by this event and regret that we will not be able to continue our commitment to our customers…
The company spent a hideous amount of money to reach a lot of customers… who adore the ads but don’t have pets.

clips.who: **Amazon.com spokeswoman**, on the value of its stake, LA Times, Nov 8, 2000[^11]

clips.q: Dig another grave in the dot-com pet cemetery.
